proposed_title: AI Act f-2026: bin deadline mktoub w-tatbi9 li khasna nverifyiw
what_happened: The EU AI Act's enacted timetable scheduled most provisions, including many obligations for high-risk systems, to apply from 2 August 2026, while some product-embedded high-risk rules have a later date. This is legal context, not confirmation of enforcement events on 7 September 2026: hosted live search returned HTTP 401 and direct official-page retrieval was blocked on 2 September 2026, so amendments, delays, guidance and actual enforcement are UNKNOWN.
key_facts: FACT — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024 and uses phased application dates.
FACT — Article 113 sets general application from 2 August 2026, with specified exceptions; prohibited-practice and AI-literacy provisions applied earlier, from 2 February 2025.
FACT — Governance and general-purpose AI provisions were scheduled from 2 August 2025, while Article 6(1) high-risk systems embedded in regulated products have a transition to 2 August 2027.
FACT — The Act distinguishes providers, deployers, importers and distributors; obligations depend on the actor and risk category, not simply on whether software uses AI.
FACT — The regulation has an extraterritorial reach in defined cases, including where output produced by a system is used in the EU; this does not mean every Moroccan AI use is automatically covered.

UNKNOWN — Whether EU lawmakers changed the timetable, which standards were finalized, what enforcement occurred, and which Moroccan organizations were affected by 7 September 2026 were not verified live.

contradictory_evidence: A simple claim that 'the whole AI Act began in August 2026' erases provisions that applied in 2025 and product-linked rules scheduled for 2027.
Vendor declarations of being 'EU AI Act compliant' are COMPANY CLAIMS unless tied to the correct role, risk classification, documentation, testing and independent evidence.
The statutory timetable is not proof that standards, national regulators or enforcement practice were fully ready by the date; those implementation facts require current records.
uncertainty: Medium to high for current status. The enacted regulation and original staged dates are stable primary material; any 2026 simplification package, postponement, finalized standard, enforcement action or Morocco-specific impact is UNKNOWN because live retrieval failed.
context: The Act uses risk tiers and actor-specific obligations rather than a single license for all AI. Moroccan exporters, service providers and technology buyers may encounter EU requirements through products, customers or outputs used in the EU, but applicability needs a case-specific legal assessment.
why_it_matters: Teams can waste money either by ignoring a rule that reaches their EU-facing work or by buying vague compliance products for systems outside the relevant category. Dates, role, use and evidence all matter.
strategic_angle: Build a verification checklist around system inventory, intended purpose, actor role, risk classification, EU nexus, documentation and human oversight. Do not announce a September 2026 enforcement milestone until EUR-Lex and regulator pages are retrieved fresh.
